purpose: City-specific official EGiB/cadastre and bounded anonymous parcel-geometry review.
assessment: The official municipal EGiB REST layer returned two Polygon geometries from a 1 km² central-city envelope (request capped at three); only native parcel ID and geometry were retained. The exact ranked WUP point and two nearby envelopes returned no features. The central sample does not establish WUP-point coverage or citywide completeness.
registryAssessment: Katowice’s official portal describes EGiB parcel records and publishes an EGiB WMS/WFS service. The ArcGIS Działki layer is polygon geometry, native EPSG:2177, supports JSON/GeoJSON query, and lists IDENT_DZ. This confirms a local cadastral service; a separate official EGiB service page discusses WFS downloads. Registry office/service presence is distinct from proof that any particular WUP locator falls on a returned parcel.

The ranked WUP point query and two nearby envelopes returned no features. A separate central-city envelope returned two safe-ID parcel polygons; those samples do not cover the WUP point.

searchQueries.result: GUGIK’s official EGiB service page explains that the register includes land/parcel data and that county WFS downloads can provide parcel geometries. Katowice’s official portal publishes its city EGiB service. The exact WUP point query returned no polygon; two central-city safe-ID samples confirm polygon geometry is retrievable elsewhere in the layer, subject to root qualification.
searchQueries.executionMethod: Separate English-language search followed by review of GUGIK and official Katowice sources; bounded anonymous requests retained only safe parcel identifiers and geometry.

officialPrimarySources.observation: Official city geospatial portal says EGiB includes parcel location, boundaries, area and land-use attributes; it publishes WMS and WFS access routes.
Official City of Katowice geodesy/cadastre office page lists EGiB record maintenance, requests for EGiB data and city WMS/WFS services.
Official ArcGIS layer metadata identifies Działki as Polygon with native WKID 2177, GeoJSON query format, maxRecordCount 1000, pagination and IDENT_DZ string field (length 36).

Official portal-linked WFS capabilities list dzialki (Działki), native CRS EPSG:2177 and GEOJSON output. Bounded GetFeature attempts at the exact WUP point and in the central sample envelope returned empty FeatureCollections; successful sample was retrieved through the REST layer.
GUGIK describes EGiB as the national ground/building register maintained by local authorities and documents WFS parcel geometry downloads, with a caveat that vector coverage may vary by county.

viewerAndServiceTrace.notes: The official city portal documents EGiB WMS/WFS. WFS GetCapabilities returned dzialki and EPSG:2177; bounded WFS GeoJSON requests returned empty collections. The REST Działki layer returned two city-center polygons with OBJECTID/IDENT_DZ requested and geometry retained. Although outSR=4326 was sent, the response coordinates remained native 2177 and had no GeoJSON CRS member; the sample was transformed locally using EPSG:2177 parameters. No ranking-point polygon was returned.

geometryEvidence.requestFilter: EPSG:2177 envelope 6572339.5,5564074.5,6573339.5,5565074.5 (central Katowice); exact point and two nearby WUP-centered envelopes returned zero features.
geometryEvidence.limitations: Two city-center polygons only. Point coverage was not established. The server response lacked numberMatched and set exceededTransferLimit=true; no completeness is inferred.

privacy: Only the source-native cadastral key IDENT_DZ and geometry are retained. OBJECTID is omitted from sample; fields relating to owners, addresses and other attributes were not requested or retained.

rootRuntimeReview.reason: Official REST GeoJSON and Esri JSON claim EPSG:4326 while returning coordinate values in native EPSG:2177 (for example x=6573053.29,y=5565132.756). Root reproduced this with two bounded Esri JSON queries: the ranked viewport is empty and the central sample returns two native-coordinate polygons under a false 4326 spatialReference, with exceededTransferLimit=true. The current runtime correctly rejects these unsupported coordinates. A truthful native CRS transport and complete enumeration/exact-ID contract remain unqualified; centroid containment is not the hold reason.
